reason: Under the schedule and feasibility lens the idea survives. It can be built and scored well before 29 Sep 10:00 UTC, and I checked that it can be implemented as a text patch. (a) Code check on experiments/exp56_x138_verbatim/exp56-x138-verbatim.ipynb, code cell 4, line 487: the 'lowdet peaks' and 'lowdet write' edits are one string-literal patch list that runs BEFORE the V1284 patch. The V1284 import is added at the top of the predict script, so `_v1284_refine`, `ds_path`, `t` and `unet_out[:, f_idx]` are all in scope where `_low` is created. I simulated the two edits in memory. Each anchor occurs exactly once: `_LOWDET.append((_low.astype(np.float32), _lsc...` and `_lc = _lc.astype(np.int16)\n`. The patched cell parses, the patched fragment compiles, and the V1284 anchors keep a count of 1. The cell-5 consumers already accept floats: load_low_detections reads low_coords as float64 (L1203), and readmit L1290 and gapfill L1445 write float(vox). No new weights or Kaggle dataset are needed, because the head is already mounted from anvithpothula/biohub-v1284-head-s075. The extra runtime is one small MLP plus a 7-point gather per frame on the >=0.3 pool, a few seconds per video, which does not threaten the 12 h limit. (b) One implementation defect: the idea, read literally, inserts `_low = _v1284_refine(...)` right after `_detect_cells_pooled`. That runs BEFORE the score lookup `_lz = _low[:,1:].astype(np.int64)`, which would silently floor the float coordinates into the score index and read wrong voxels. The fix is to refine at append time (see fix_if_any). (c) Validation step (2) cannot be scheduled. No x138 lab cache on the 199 videos exists. The planned x138 train-run in v_divisions_divins-x138-lab-retune_schedule.json dumps only the inputs to the short-track and linefit stages. READMIT and GAPFILL run inside the cell-5 relink chain and need UNet features at dump time. So a lab replay would need both the refined and unrefined pools dumped in that run, plus a cell-5 replay from the ILP graph: about 3-5 h of extra engineering (a guess) on a run that is itself only about 0.6-0.7 likely to go ahead. The honest checks are therefore only (1), structural checks on the dummy clips, and (3), a no-harm LB rider. That rider has little power: with per-score noise of about 0.003, the difference between two scores has an SD of about 0.004 (a guess). A truly neutral change then passes 'public >= F1 - 0.001' only about 60% of the time, and a +0.0003 effect cannot be seen. This is a value problem (the sibling v_github-intel_lowdet-refine_value.json refuted it on value), not a schedule problem. (d) Numbers checked: 1,337 readmitted of 121,777 raw nodes on the dummy clips (CONTEXT.md L1515); head +0.007 on the x138 base (CONTEXT.md L1495-1504); READMIT radius 4 um / min score 0.965, GAPFILL min score 0.5 / EXCLUDE 2.0 um / MAX_ADDED_FRAC 0.03, LOWDET 0.3 (x138 cell 0, L92-105). The head's bounded shift is below 2 um, so pool duplicates of kept nodes stay inside EXCLUDE, whether refined or not.
fix_if_any: Implement it as tools/build_probe_kernel.py `--patch lowrefine`, added to BASES['x138']['patches'], with two exact-once string replacements in the x138 code cell 4 source. (1) Replace `_LOWDET.append((_low.astype(np.float32), _lsc.astype(np.float32)))` with `_LOWDET.append((_v1284_refine(ds_path, t, _low, unet_out[:, f_idx]).astype(np.float32), _lsc.astype(np.float32)))`. This refines AFTER the score lookup, so the lookup keeps using the integer peaks without needing a copy. (2) Delete the line `                _lc = _lc.astype(np.int16)\n`. Raise an error if either anchor count is not 1. Tests: with the patch off the output must be byte-identical to exp56; the patched predict-script fragment must compile; check that the V1284 anchor counts are unchanged; unit-test refine on a synthetic integer pool (moves <2 um, float32, frame column unchanged). Optional private-safety variant: refine only pool peaks with score >= 0.965, i.e. the readmit-eligible peaks that are in-distribution for the head. The 0.5-0.965 gapfill peaks are out of distribution for the head (it was trained on >= 0.965 detections), so this variant keeps the change aligned with where the head was trained. Dummy-run gate before any submission: raw node count == exp56 (121,777), the LOWDET peak counts identical, readmitted count 1,337 +-5%, gapfill node count +-10%, no 'readmit skipped' / 'REPAIR FAILED' lines, and only readmit or gapfill nodes and their incident edges differ (use scratchpad/cmp57.py against out_exp56). Ship only as a rider in a probe that is being submitted anyway, never on its own slot.
realistic_public_gain: +0.0003 (0 to +0.001); cannot be seen at LB noise 0.003
realistic_private_gain: +0.0002 to +0.0003 (sign uncertain for the refined gapfill peaks, which are out of distribution for the head; the variant that refines only readmit-eligible peaks is safer)

(3) 26 Sep after the 00:00 UTC quota reset, realistically 06:00-09:00 UTC when Vitalii is at his laptop: Vitalii pushes the kernel to vitaliineibauer (T4, same docker pin as exp56) and runs it on the 4 dummy clips, 0.5-0.7 GPU-h out of the fresh 30 GPU-h. sasyami could do this run on 25 Sep evening, but friend A's availability is uncertain, so it is not on the critical path. (4) Next 30 min, laptop: download the output, run cmp57.py-style gate checks against out_exp56, optionally a leaky 4-clip official score via tools/csv2geff.py and tools/score_geffs.py. (5) 26 Sep ~09:00-10:00 UTC: user OK, Vitalii submits, using 1 of the 5 slots for 26 Sep, ideally as a rider inside the F1' probe that is being submitted anyway. (6) Scored 26 Sep ~17:00-20:00 UTC (7-10 h latency). Slack to 29 Sep 10:00 UTC is about 62 h, so two full-day slips still fit. Lab replay step (2) is left out: no x138 199-video cache exists, and piggybacking on the divins-retune train-run would need the refined and unrefined pools dumped at run time plus a cell-5 replay (+3-5 h engineering, a guess). P(scored by the deadline | the team spends a slot or rider on it) is about 0.9. The only real risk is priority: an invisible change competes for 21 shared slots and user approval.
